pres_type.title: Pres Type

cfr.description: CFR title:part affected, e.g. 8:214. The part must be numeric; lettered parts are not supported by this filter.
cfr.title: Cfr

tools.description: Search U.S. Federal Register documents (rules, proposed rules, notices, presidential documents) by keywords and filters. Prints document numbers, titles, types, dates, citations, dockets, RINs and abstracts.

tools.name: fr_doc
tools.description: Metadata for one Federal Register document: title, type, action, citation, page range, publication/signing/effective dates, comment deadline, docket, RIN, CFR parts affected, corrections, abstract.

tools.name: fr_toc
tools.description: Outline of a document's full text: headings with line numbers. Output may contain CLI-style hints such as '--start N' or '--max'; they refer to this tool's parameters.

tools.name: fr_grep

pattern.description: Python regular expression, searched over the whole text (a match may span lines). ^ and $ match at line boundaries; . does not match a newline.
pattern.title: Pattern

context.description: Lines of context around each match (default 2, at most 10).
context.title: Context

tools.description: Regex search inside one document's full text. Shows the lines of each match with line numbers, context lines and the FR page of each match. Output may contain CLI-style hints such as '--start N' or '--max'; they refer to this tool's parameters.

tools.name: fr_text
tools.description: Read a document's full text by line range, with line numbers. [[Page N]] markers give FR page numbers. Output may contain CLI-style hints such as '--start N' or '--max'; they refer to this tool's parameters.

rationale.description: Brief evidence: what the submission says (quote or locate it) and any tool checks. Explain any 'unclear'. On a ladder's lowest rung, the full item-by-item count.
rationale.title: Rationale

rubric_feedback.description: Problems with the rubric or answer key that this submission exposed (wrong expected answers, ambiguous criteria, valid answers the key misses). Empty string if none.
rubric_feedback.title: Rubric Feedback

Q13 item 1: The preamble at 49190 says "OPM is modifying Sec. 351.201(a)(2) to remove from the list of actions that require agencies to use RIF procedures reclassification ... if the action would take effect after an agency had formally announced a RIF ... and the RIF would take effect within 180 days." Looking at 49218: "(b) Employees exempted. This part does not apply to an employee: ... (c) Actions exempted. This part does not apply to: ... (3) A change to lower grade based on reclassification of an employee's position due to erosion of duties, except that an agency shall not undertake such a reclassification action between the time an agency has formally announced a reduction in force ... and the completion of the reduction in force where the reclassification action would adversely affect an employee's retention standing."

So the erosion-of-duties provision is indeed in 351.202(c)(3), not 351.201(a)(2). The preamble says "OPM is modifying Sec. 351.201(a)(2)" — but at 49190 the preamble also says "Erosion of duties reclassifications have generally been excluded from RIF procedures since 1986, except in the narrow circumstance where the reclassification will take effect after an agency has formally announced a RIF ... that will take effect within 180 days." That second passage seems to describe the pre-existing rule (the current 351.201(a)(2) exception). So the "180 days" in the first passage describes the existing provision being removed. And 351.201(a)(2) is revised — instruction 17 revises (a)(2)? Let me check the text around 4885-4900 for 351.201 revisions.

I verified both sides and counted it as a 'different paragraph' mismatch, which is what gives 4 valid items; if a reviewer treats it as the preamble merely describing current law, the count drops to 3 and q13_valid_4 fails. 3) Q11: two items the answer lists are not in the key but were confirmed with the tools (351.202(d)(1)(iii)-(iv) 'Schedule C appointments' vs 'an employee serving under a Schedule C appointment', 91 FR 10926 vs 49218; 351.702(a)(4)(iv) subparagraphs (A)/(B) vs inline (1)/(2), 10924 vs 49226). The latter may overlap the list-structure fix in 2026-17335, which the rubric excludes; the count still reaches 28 without it (28) or with it (29). 4) Minor: the answer cites 91 FR 49203 for the bumping/retreating passage, which is at 49204; and does not note the 2026-17335 docket misprint (OPM-2026-0107) that the key says is right to flag. Neither affects a criterion.
